mutant.description: The TO and my own prior surprise report both asserted the :873 memoization rule was the gate blocker. Rather than accept that framing, I tested the competing hypothesis directly: fix ONLY the unused import, leave :873 completely alone, and re-run the repo-wide gate. If the memo were the blocker the gate must still fail; if the import were the blocker it must pass with the memo warning still printed.
mutant.expected: If the stated attribution were right: rc=1 with the memoization error still failing. If my re-attribution were right: rc=0 with the memoization line still printed as a WARNING.
mutant.observed: rc=0, '1 problem (0 errors, 1 warning)', the :873 memoization line STILL PRESENT in the output. The stated attribution is falsified and the re-attribution confirmed by the gate itself. Independently corroborated from the resolved eslint config: preserve-manual-memoization severity 1 (warning), no-unused-imports severity 2 (error), and `lint` carries no --max-warnings so warnings alone cannot fail it.

determinism.method: The gate is a deterministic static analyzer over a fixed tree, not a timing- or network-dependent instrument; the before (rc=1, 1 error 1 warning) and after (rc=0, 0 errors 1 warning) runs were each executed on the full tree with the same command, and the single surviving warning is byte-identical across runs.
determinism.observed: Stable: same command, same tree, same output modulo the one removed error. No run-to-run variance observed.

surprises: The blocker was misattributed at the source and I am the source: my OPAL_ANALYST.EXP1 surprise #1 named :873/preserve-manual-memoization as the failing rule, and the TO was written from that. The real error was an unused import. I reported the co-located WARNING that eslint printed with a large code frame instead of the terse ERROR line above it -- the visually louder finding was not the operative one. Cost here was zero because the true fix was strictly safer than the feared one, but the same misread in the other direction would have sent a seat into memoization semantics for no reason.
